nodes.name: PS-Disc — Schedule Trigger
nodes.notes: Configurable recurring trigger for live government discovery. Defaults to every 6 hours -- change the interval in this node's parameters (or via PERMITSIGNAL_DISCOVERY_CRON, see README) without touching any other node. Deactivate this node (or the whole workflow) to stop scheduled runs; PS-Disc — Manual Trigger still allows on-demand testing while deactivated.

nodes.name: PS-Disc — Manual Trigger
nodes.notes: On-demand execution for testing discovery without waiting for the schedule. Feeds the same downstream path as the schedule trigger.

nodes.name: PS-Disc — Build Discovery Request
nodes.notes: Builds the /discover/provo request body from environment variables so discovery controls are configurable without editing the workflow. All four fields map 1:1 to backend.app.main.DiscoverProvoRequest -- no invented parameters. Defaults: reference_date=today, live_enrichment=false, sync_to_supabase=true, dry_run=false (matching the API's own defaults).

nodes.name: PS-Disc — Discover Provo
nodes.notes: POST {{ $env.PERMITSIGNAL_API_URL }}/discover/provo -- the existing Phase 2 live discovery boundary (backend/app/main.py). This single call performs live Provo government discovery (backend.app.collectors.provo), registry/idempotency filtering (document_registry), document download, and the full existing 7-stage pipeline (applicant/company enrichment, approval-action intelligence, commercial/qualified-lead intelligence, Supabase persistence) for every newly discovered packet. No discovery, extraction, enrichment, or persistence logic is duplicated in n8n. continueOnFail is enabled so a request failure (unreachable API, timeout, 5xx) produces an item this workflow can branch on instead of aborting the execution silently.

nodes.name: PS-Disc — Classify Result
nodes.notes: Routes on the actual /discover/provo response so n8n's execution history makes the outcome obvious at a glance: request failure (unreachable/timeout/5xx), malformed response (no status field), successful discovery with per-document pipeline errors, successful discovery with zero new records, or successful discovery with new records ingested. Registry/idempotency itself is decided entirely server-side (document_registry) -- this only classifies the response for visibility.

nodes.name: PS-Disc — ERROR: Discovery API Request Failed
nodes.notes: Reached when the HTTP call to /discover/provo itself failed -- unreachable backend, timeout, connection refused, or a non-2xx status (including a 500 from an unhandled discovery exception, e.g. the Provo site or Playwright being unavailable). The real error is surfaced, never swallowed.

string.name: error_message
string.value: ={{ $json.error?.message || $json.error?.description || JSON.stringify($json.error) || 'Unknown error calling PermitSignal discovery API.' }}

nodes.name: PS-Disc — ERROR: Malformed Discovery Response
nodes.notes: Reached when the API responded but the body has no 'status' field -- an unexpected response shape (e.g. a proxy/gateway page instead of the FastAPI JSON response). Treated as a distinct failure from a normal API error so a silent contract change is never mistaken for success.

string.name: error_message
string.value: Discovery API response had no 'status' field -- unexpected response shape.

nodes.name: PS-Disc — WARNING: Pipeline Errors During Ingestion
nodes.notes: Discovery itself succeeded, but one or more newly discovered packets failed during download/pipeline ingestion (discovery_orchestrator.ingest_document() catches per-document failures so one bad packet never aborts the batch). Surfaced as a warning, not a false success -- the errors array is the real per-document error list from the backend.

nodes.name: PS-Disc — SUCCESS: No New Records
nodes.notes: Discovery ran successfully and found nothing new -- the expected, common outcome on most scheduled runs once the registry is caught up. Distinguished from the new-records case so execution history doesn't look identical to a run that actually ingested something.

nodes.name: PS-Disc — SUCCESS: New Records Found
nodes.notes: Discovery found new government packets with zero per-document pipeline errors. When dry_run=false (the production default), every new packet was already downloaded and run through the existing pipeline server-side (applicant/company enrichment, approval-action intelligence, commercial lead intelligence, Supabase persistence) -- ingested_count/ingested reflect the real outcome. When dry_run=true (manual testing), new records were discovered and registered but intentionally not ingested -- check the dry_run field before treating ingested_count as final. This node only surfaces real backend counts; it never duplicates the intelligence payload.
